extracted.intended_audience: readers of Nature (scientists, engineers, and informed public)
extracted.subtask_description: Brief report of changes and key provisions in the revised Institution of Electrical Engineers wiring rules (early-20th-century context), plus other short scientific/news items. Focuses on standards for conductors, insulation tests, equipment classification, and scope by voltage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of wiring rules (voltage limit)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The rules apply only for voltages up to 250 volts, the Board of Trade rules being appended and used for the higher pressures."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the IEE wiring rules for installations up to 250 V; for voltages from 250 V to 650 V, apply the Board of Trade rules (appended); higher voltages handled by other authorities (Home Office referenced in text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for copper conductors (Electrical Standards Committee)
rubrics_metrics.description: "The standard for copper conductors is now that of the Electrical Standards Committee instead of Mathiessen's standard."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt the Electrical Standards Committee (E.S.C.) specifications for copper conductor dimensions/weights/resistance in place of the older Mathiessen standard when specifying or testing conductors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insulation tests modified (bending test omitted)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Insulation tests are also modified in that the 'bending' test has been omitted, though an increase in the length of time for which the pressure test is applied takes its place."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove bending test to avoid mechanical rupture risks when flexing cables; substitute by extending duration of the pressure (dielectric) test to ensure insulation integrity under prolonged stress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance of bare conductors under conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: "Bare conductors also are allowed under special conditions."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bare conductors may be permissible but only under specified special conditions (details not provided in the excerpt); follow the rules' stated conditions and limitations when permitting bare conductors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Switch casing insulation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: "Switches of more than 5 amperes at 125 volts when placed in cases are to have their cases lined with asbestos."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For switches rated over 5 A at 125 V that are enclosed, provide asbestos lining in the case for insulation/safety as required by the rules (historical material requirement; modern standards differ).

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification/organization of electrical apparatus in the rules
rubrics_metrics.description: "Dynamos and motors are now placed under separate headings, but transformers are no longer kept separate, being under a combined heading with resistances and choking coils."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When consulting or applying the rules, note the reorganized grouping: treat dynamos and motors distinctly; treat transformers together with resistances and choking coils under a combined heading for classification and applicable provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electrical Standards Committee resistance/weight definition (E.S.C. standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: "A wire one metre long and weighing one gramme having a resistance of 01539 E.S.C. standard ohms at 60° F."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statement defines the E.S.C. reference standard for copper conductor resistance and weight (used as the basis for conductor specifications and comparisons). Use the E.S.C. numerical reference when specifying conductor resistance at 60°F per the rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tabby-cat classification by stripe pattern
rubrics_metrics.description: "English domestic cats, whatever their colour may be, and whether they belong to 'Manx,' 'Persian,' or 'ordinary' breeds, are shown by their pattern of stripes to be referable to two distinct kinds, known as the 'striped' and 'blotched' tabbies."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the pattern of stripes (striped vs blotched) as a primary phenotypic criterion to distinguish these two categories of domestic cats in taxonomic or descriptive work; this is presented as the observable basis for classification in the exhibitor's notes.
